memory_candidates.content: Merging a new extension's EXTENSION.md into .claude/CLAUDE.md (merge_targets.claudemd) directly counts toward verify-deploy.sh Gate 20's orchestrator eager-load-total regression check (measure-eager-context.sh --check against orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes), because the predicted assembled CLAUDE.md is part of that eager-load total. A brand-new extension's EXTENSION.md -- even a short, well-scoped one -- can push the total over baseline on its own. Check this gate (bash .claude/scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check, or verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 20) after writing a new EXTENSION.md and before considering that phase done; if over, relocate duplicated detail to the extension's own non-eager context/ files (which are NOT eager-loaded) and keep only a short pointer in EXTENSION.md, following this codebase's established 'always trim, never bump' precedent rather than moving the baseline.

check-extension-docs.sh's script-reference check flags ANY .sh filename literally mentioned in an extension's docs (EXTENSION.md/README.md) that is not also present in that extension's manifest provides.scripts array -- it does not distinguish 'this extension ships X' from 'this extension deliberately does NOT ship X'. When documenting a deliberately-dropped script or hook by name (e.g. explaining why a gap-3 context-injection script was not built), describe the mechanism without writing the literal filename/.sh string anywhere in the extension's own files, or the doc-lint gate fails on a true negative.
